headline: Bruins get embarrassed in a lifeless shutout against the Kings
morning_brew: Tuesday night at the Garden was an absolute disaster. I watched the Bruins drop a 3-0 decision to the Kings, and honestly, the only thing more lifeless than the offense was my own mood by the final horn. We couldn't buy a goal to save our lives, and getting blanked at home while the Kings snap a four-game skid is exactly the kind of result that makes you want to throw your remote through the screen. It is a tough look for a team that is supposed to be contending, and right now, the consistency is nonexistent.

This team is officially in a rut with a three-game losing streak that feels like it has been going on for a month. We have to find a way to generate some actual offense instead of just skating around and praying for a miracle. My neighbor Rick is already four days into his deep-dive dossier on trade demands and locker room chemistry, and while I usually ignore his wild theories, it is hard to argue that something isn't fundamentally broken when you get shut out by an opponent that was begging to lose. We need to wake up before this whole month slips away into the gutter.

Looking ahead to tonight, we have a quick turnaround with a trip to Detroit to face the Red Wings. The schedule doesn't care about our feelings, and we have to get back on the ice at Little Caesars Arena and prove that Tuesday was just a one-off performance from a team that forgot how to play hockey. It is time for the top lines to actually dictate the pace and get some pucks past their goalie, because another performance like the one we just witnessed would be plain unacceptable. I'll be tuned in at seven-thirty, nursing a Dunks and hoping for a bounce-back effort that finally gives us something to cheer about.

news_digest.headline: Darcy Kuemper stops 29 shots for 40th career shutout in Kings' 3-0 win over Bruins
news_digest.dans_take: Getting shut out by a team that was riding a four-game losing streak is a new low, even for us.

news_digest.headline: Bruins bring 3-game losing streak into matchup with the Red Wings
news_digest.dans_take: We need to treat Detroit like a must-win game or this losing skid is going to get even uglier, and I really don't want to hear Rick talk about it.
